# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, mapping each light color to the wire color that must be cut. I can only communicate via gestures, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see anything I send. Deaf can see the bomb (the light) but not hear or receive gestures from Blind directly in a useful way — wait, Deaf can see gestures too.

The turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. So this round: Blind spoke first (I haven't seen it yet, it'll arrive next round), then me, then Deaf.

Since I go before Deaf in this round, and Deaf can see my gestures, I could try to send the manual mapping to Deaf via gestures. Deaf will then see the bomb's light color and know which wire to cut - but Deaf cannot touch the bomb! Deaf must relay the cut instruction to Blind, but Deaf cannot speak either... wait, checking table: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can Deaf speak? The table only lists what Deaf cannot do: hear, touch. So Deaf CAN speak.

So the chain: I (Mute) gesture the manual to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb's light, looks up the wire color, and speaks the wire color to Blind (Blind can hear, per elimination - Blind cannot see or hear... wait let me check Blind's row: cannot see a color/gesture/printed thing. Nothing about hearing. So Blind CAN hear.

So plan: I need to teach Deaf the full mapping via gestures, since I don't know what the bomb shows yet. Let me encode the manual using gesture symbols representing colors, since Deaf can see gestures.

I'll assign gesture symbols to colors: blue=👍, green=👎, red=✊, white=✋, yellow=☝

Let me send the pairs to Deaf now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see: display shows 0, light is yellow, five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. I received your gestures but don't know your code yet - please gesture one symbol per wire number so I can map them, or gesture a single symbol for yes/confirm if this matches the manual.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is yellow. Wires 1 to 5 in order: white, red, yellow, green, blue.

I now know the key facts: light is yellow, and per the manual, yellow → cut wire color blue. The wires in order are: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue. So the wire to cut is wire #5 (blue).

Deaf doesn't know my gesture code yet, but Blind already relayed the same info to me via speech (since Blind heard Deaf speak it, presumably). Wait, actually Blind says "Deaf reports" - meaning Deaf spoke this info and Blind heard it. So Blind already has the raw bomb data too.

My job now: confirm to Deaf my code, and more importantly, I should tell Blind directly which wire to cut - but I can't speak, only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I cannot reach Blind directly at all. I must go through Deaf, who can speak to Blind.

So I need to gesture to Deaf the mapping so Deaf can compute it themselves, or just gesture the answer directly using wire position. Let me confirm my color code first, and also send position-based confirmation. Simplest: gesture the wire number to cut using my established code isn't set up for numbers. Let me define numbers via count of same symbol, or use distinct symbols 1-5.

I'll gesture a fresh clear mapping: for numbers 1-5 use ☝✌🤟✋🖐 (finger counts), confirming wire 5 (blue) is the one to cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I think I understand: you are numbering wires 1 to 5 using finger-count symbols, then giving a second symbol per wire meaning something like an instruction. So wire 1 gets thumbs up, wire 2 gets thumbs down, wire 3 gets fist, wire 4 gets index finger, wire 5 gets thumbs up. If thumbs up means cut and thumbs down means do not cut, gesture a single thumbs up to me now to confirm. If wrong, gesture thumbs down instead.

Deaf misunderstood my encoding - they think it's a per-wire cut/don't-cut instruction rather than my color code (👍=blue, 👎=green, ✊=red, ☝=yellow, actually wait let me recheck what I sent).

I need to reconsider. My original color code was: blue=👍, green=👎, red=✊, white=✋, yellow=☝. Then I sent pairs meaning "finger-count number → color": 🖐(5 wires), then ☝👍 (1→blue), ✌👎 (2→green), 🤟✊ (3→red), ✋☝ (4→yellow), 🖐👍 (5→blue).

Wait, that's wrong on my part - I mislabeled. Let me redo cleanly: I wanted to say wire 5 should be cut, and wire 5 is blue, which per manual (yellow light → cut blue) is correct. But my mapping got confused with white=✋ vs wire4=✋.

Deaf's confusion: they think 👍=cut, 👎=don't cut. That's incorrect but I can simplify - just confirm THIS specific answer only, not the general code, since we only need one answer this round. Let me not confirm their wrong theory, but instead send a clean simple gesture: just point to wire 5 directly.

I'll gesture the number 5 (🖐) alone, meaning "cut wire number 5". That's simplest given Deaf already knows wire order from their own bomb view.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

Deaf wants a clean single gesture indicating the wire number. Since Deaf already knows the light is yellow and the wire order (1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue), and my manual says yellow → cut blue, the correct wire is #5. I'll send just the five-finger gesture alone as requested.
